learningObjective: Precisely state the representable value ranges of INT8 (signed) and INT4 (signed) for symmetric quantization.

canonicalClaims.claim: In symmetric quantization, INT8 uses [-127, 127] and INT4 uses [-7, 7], sacrificing one representable value (the negative extreme) to keep the range symmetric around zero and simplify GEMM implementations.
conditions: The quantization framework follows the standard symmetric convention.
nonImplications: Does not imply asymmetric quantization is inferior; it gains one representable value at the cost of a zero-point offset in the GEMM.
Does not imply the sacrificed value never appears — asymmetric quantization can use it.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Two's-complement INT8 has range [-128, 127]; +128 does not exist.

misconceptions.claim: Symmetric quantization uses the full two's-complement range [-128, 127].
misconceptions.whyWrong: Symmetric quantization sacrifices -128 to keep the range symmetric [-127, 127].

misconceptions.claim: INT8 quantization always uses unsigned [0, 255] representation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both signed [-127, 127] and unsigned [0, 255] variants exist, driven by the quantization scheme (symmetric vs. asymmetric).

misconceptions.claim: Symmetric quantization is always preferred over asymmetric because it wastes only one value.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For activations with a natural zero point (post-ReLU), asymmetric quantization is often more accurate; the choice is workload-dependent.

implementationFacts: TensorRT default INT8: symmetric per-tensor for activations, symmetric per-channel for weights.
PyTorch's `torch.ao.quantization` supports both symmetric and asymmetric configurations.
performanceScenarios: Symmetric INT8 GEMM avoids the extra bias term needed by asymmetric quantization, simplifying kernels.
